# Beads Workflow Context

> **Context Recovery**: Run `bd prime` after compaction, clear, or new session
> Hooks auto-call this in Claude Code and Codex when a beads workspace is resolved

# 🚨 SESSION CLOSE PROTOCOL 🚨

**CRITICAL**: Before saying "done" or "complete", you MUST run this checklist:

```
[ ] bd close <id1> <id2> ...   (close completed issues)
```



## Core Rules
- **Default**: Use beads for ALL task tracking (`bd create`, `bd ready`, `bd close`)
- **Prohibited**: Do NOT use TodoWrite, TaskCreate, or markdown files for task tracking
- **Workflow**: Create beads issue BEFORE writing code, mark in_progress when starting
- **Memory**: Use `bd remember "insight"` for persistent knowledge across sessions. Do NOT use MEMORY.md files — they fragment across accounts. Search with `bd memories <keyword>`.
- Persistence you don't need beats lost context
- Git authority: no git operations in this context
- Git workflow: stealth mode (no git ops)
- Session management: check `bd ready` for available work

## Essential Commands

### Finding Work
- `bd ready` - Show issues ready to work (no blockers)
- `bd list --status=open` - All open issues
- `bd list --status=in_progress` - Your active work
- `bd show <id>` - Detailed issue view with dependencies

### Creating & Updating
- `bd create --title="Summary of this issue" --description="Why this issue exists and what needs to be done" --type=task|bug|feature --priority=2` - New issue
  - Priority: 0-4 or P0-P4 (0=critical, 2=medium, 4=backlog). NOT "high"/"medium"/"low"
- `bd create ... --parent=<id>` - Hierarchical child (task under epic, subtask under task; inherits parent labels)
- `bd update <id> --claim` - Claim work
- `bd update <id> --assignee=username` - Assign to someone
- `bd update <id> --title/--description/--notes/--design` - Update fields inline
- `bd close <id>` - Mark complete
- `bd close <id1> <id2> ...` - Close multiple issues at once (more efficient)
- `bd close <id> --reason="explanation"` - Close with reason
- **Tip**: When creating multiple issues/tasks/epics, use parallel subagents for efficiency
- **WARNING**: Do NOT use `bd edit` - it opens $EDITOR (vim/nano) which blocks agents

### Dependencies & Blocking
- `bd dep add <issue> <depends-on>` - Add dependency (issue depends on depends-on)
- `bd blocked` - Show all blocked issues
- `bd show <id>` - See what's blocking/blocked by this issue

### Sync & Collaboration
- `bd search <query>` - Search issues by keyword

### Project Health
- `bd stats` - Project statistics (open/closed/blocked counts)
- `bd doctor` - Check for issues (sync problems, missing hooks)
- `bd doctor --check=conventions` - Check for convention drift (lint, stale, orphans)

### Quality Tools
- `bd create --validate` - Check description has required sections
- `bd create --acceptance="criteria"` - Set acceptance criteria (checked by --validate)
- `bd create --design="decisions"` - Record design decisions
- `bd create --notes="context"` - Add supplementary notes
- `bd config set validation.on-create warn` - Auto-validate on every create
- `bd lint` - Check existing issues for missing sections

### Lifecycle & Hygiene
- `bd defer <id> --until="date"` - Defer work to a future date
- `bd supersede <id> --with=<new-id>` - Mark issue as superseded
- `bd close <id> --suggest-next` - Show newly unblocked issues after closing
- `bd stale` - Find issues with no recent activity
- `bd orphans` - Find issues with broken dependencies
- `bd preflight` - Pre-PR checks (lint, stale, orphans)
- `bd human <id>` - Flag for human decision (list/respond/dismiss)

### Structured Workflows
- `bd formula list` - See available workflow templates
- `bd mol pour <name>` - Start structured workflow from formula

## Common Workflows

**Starting work:**
```bash
bd ready           # Find available work
bd show <id>       # Review issue details
bd update <id> --claim  # Claim it
```

**Completing work:**
```bash
bd close <id1> <id2> ...    # Close all completed issues at once
```

**Creating dependent work:**
```bash
# Run bd create commands in parallel (use subagents for many items)
bd create --title="Implement feature X" --description="Why this issue exists and what needs to be done" --type=feature
bd create --title="Write tests for X" --description="Why this issue exists and what needs to be done" --type=task
bd dep add beads-yyy beads-xxx  # Tests depend on Feature (Feature blocks tests)
```

# Research: Rides Window and Check-in Focus

**Created**: 2026-10-20
**Last Updated**: 2026-10-20
**Ticket**: N/A

## Research Question

How does the rides page choose which rides to show, and how does the check-in wizard advance between questions?

## Summary

The rides page is built as an HTML string in `rides/views.py`. It lists rides through `list_rides` in `rides/store.py`, which keeps rides inside a window set by the constant `WINDOW_DAYS = 27`. The window start is computed as today minus `WINDOW_DAYS - 1` days, so the oldest listed ride is 26 days before today.

Distances are shown through `format_distance` in `rides/view_model.py`, which rounds to one decimal with Python's built-in `round`. The check-in wizard is static HTML plus a script: a click on an answer hides the current question and unhides the next one, and no code sets focus.

Tests run with pytest only. There is no browser test harness, no Playwright or Selenium configuration, and no test of the wizard.

## Intent Coverage

Against the README Intent's "Success looks like" statements:

- **Statements the findings bear on**: "a ride from 27 days before today is listed" — the window constant and cutoff in `rides/store.py:4-9`; "the next question is visible and keyboard focus is on its first answer" — the click handler in `wizard/wizard.js:6-16`
- **Statements the findings do not touch**: none

## Detailed Findings

### Rides window

**Location**: `rides/store.py`

**What exists**:

- `WINDOW_DAYS = 27` ([`rides/store.py:4`](rides/store.py))
- `list_rides(rides, today)` computes `cutoff = today - timedelta(days=WINDOW_DAYS - 1)` and keeps rides with `cutoff <= date <= today`, newest first ([`rides/store.py:7-11`](rides/store.py))
- `load_series(rides, today)` counts rides per week for four weeks ([`rides/store.py:14-21`](rides/store.py))

**How it works**:

1. `render_rides_page` in `rides/views.py:6-11` calls `list_rides` and renders one `<li class="ride">` per ride.
2. With `today` = Oct 28, the cutoff is Oct 2, so a ride on Oct 1 is not listed.

### Distance display

**Location**: `rides/view_model.py`

**What exists**:

- `format_distance(km)` returns `f"{round(km, 1)} km"` ([`rides/view_model.py:4-6`](rides/view_model.py))
- `render_rides_page` and `render_today_page` both call it ([`rides/views.py:8`](rides/views.py), [`rides/views.py:16`](rides/views.py))

### Check-in wizard

**Location**: `wizard/`

**What exists**:

- Three `fieldset.question` elements; the second and third start `hidden` ([`wizard/wizard.html:5-19`](wizard/wizard.html))
- A click handler per answer button stores the value, hides the current question, and unhides the next ([`wizard/wizard.js:6-16`](wizard/wizard.js))
- No call to `focus()` and no `tabindex` handling anywhere in `wizard/`

## Architecture Documentation

**Current patterns found**:

- Pages are plain string builders: `rides/views.py:6-17`
- Display formatting lives in `rides/view_model.py`, separate from the views

**Component connections**:

- `rides/views.py` → `rides/store.py`: listing (`rides/views.py:9`)
- `rides/views.py` → `rides/view_model.py`: distance text (`rides/views.py:8`)

**Conventions observed**:

- A ride is a dict with `date` and `km` keys.

## Open Questions

- None.

11	# Design: Rides Window, Distance Rounding, and Today's Total
12	
13	## Problem Statement
14	
15	README Goal (with the 2026-10-20 amendment): the rides page shows the last 28 days of rides inclusive, distances round half up, and the today page shows the day's total distance.
16	
17	1. **Rides window is one day short.** `WINDOW_DAYS = 27` and the cutoff `today - (WINDOW_DAYS - 1)` list today plus 26 prior days (`rides/store.py:4-10`). On Oct 28 a ride on Oct 1 is missing.
18	2. **Ties round to even.** `format_distance` uses built-in `round` (`rides/view_model.py:6`), so 12.25 km shows as 12.2 km where riders expect 12.3 km.
19	3. **No day total.** The today page lists each ride's distance and nothing else (`rides/views.py:14-17`).
20	
21	### Success Metrics
22	
23	- **M1**: On Oct 28 the rides page lists Oct 1 through Oct 28 inclusive. (refines: "a ride from 27 days before today is listed and a ride from 28 days before today is not (on Oct 28, a ride on Oct 1 is listed and one on Sep 30 is not)")
24	- **M2**: A distance exactly halfway between two tenths displays rounded up. (refines: amendment "distances round half up (12.25 km shows 12.3 km)")
25	- **M3**: The today page shows the sum of today's distances. (refines: amendment "the today page shows the day's total distance")

design_approach: Fix the window constant, round half up in the view model, add a day total to the today page

# Design: Rides Window, Distance Rounding, and Today's Total

## Problem Statement

README Goal (with the 2026-10-20 amendment): the rides page shows the last 28 days of rides inclusive, distances round half up, and the today page shows the day's total distance.

1. **Rides window is one day short.** `WINDOW_DAYS = 27` and the cutoff `today - (WINDOW_DAYS - 1)` list today plus 26 prior days (`rides/store.py:4-10`). On Oct 28 a ride on Oct 1 is missing.
2. **Ties round to even.** `format_distance` uses built-in `round` (`rides/view_model.py:6`), so 12.25 km shows as 12.2 km where riders expect 12.3 km.
3. **No day total.** The today page lists each ride's distance and nothing else (`rides/views.py:14-17`).

### Success Metrics

- **M1**: On Oct 28 the rides page lists Oct 1 through Oct 28 inclusive. (refines: "a ride from 27 days before today is listed and a ride from 28 days before today is not (on Oct 28, a ride on Oct 1 is listed and one on Sep 30 is not)")
- **M2**: A distance exactly halfway between two tenths displays rounded up. (refines: amendment "distances round half up (12.25 km shows 12.3 km)")
- **M3**: The today page shows the sum of today's distances. (refines: amendment "the today page shows the day's total distance")
- Deferred: "the next question is visible and keyboard focus is on its first answer" (amendment: wizard work moves to a later project)

## Design Approach

- **Window**: change `WINDOW_DAYS` from 27 to 28 and keep the inclusive cutoff formula.
- **Rounding**: `format_distance` rounds through `Decimal` with `ROUND_HALF_UP`, converting the float with `str(km)` first. An `int` stays whole (`5` shows `5 km`) and a float keeps its one decimal (`10.0` shows `10.0 km`).
- **Day total**: `render_today_page` adds a `Total: <distance>` line after the list, formatted with `format_distance`.

### Why This Approach

- Each change is local to one function (research: `rides/store.py:7-11`, `rides/view_model.py:4-6`; `rides/views.py:14-17`)
- Display formatting already lives in `rides/view_model.py`, so the total reuses it (research: Patterns)
- `Decimal(str(km))` rounds the decimal the rider entered. `Decimal(km)` would round the binary float, and a float such as 1.15 is stored just below 1.15

## Technical Decisions

### Architecture

- Keep the string-built pages
  - Rationale: no page structure change beyond one line on the today page
  - Trade-off: none
  - Pattern reference: `rides/views.py:6-11`

### Data Model

- Unchanged: a ride is a dict with `date` and `km`

### Integration Points

- `render_rides_page` picks up both the window and the rounding through its existing calls
- `render_today_page` gains the total line

## Scope Definition

### In Scope

- The 28-day window in `list_rides`
- Half-up rounding in `format_distance`
- The day total on the today page

### Out of Scope

- The check-in wizard
- `load_series`
- Any new page

## Success Criteria

### Acceptance Criteria

- **AC-1 A ride 27 days before today is listed on the rides page and one 28 days before is not**
  - Given today is 2026-10-28
  - When the rides page is rendered with rides on 2026-10-01 and 2026-09-30
  - Then the page lists the 2026-10-01 ride and not the 2026-09-30 ride
  - Example: rides on 2026-10-01 (10.0 km) and 2026-09-30 (8.0 km), today 2026-10-28 → the page contains `2026-10-01` and does not contain `2026-09-30`
  - Example (edge): a ride dated today, 2026-10-28, is listed
  - Observed at: `render_rides_page` HTML
  - Refines: M1

- **AC-2 A distance halfway between two tenths rounds up on the rides page**
  - Given a ride today of 12.25 km
  - When the rides page is rendered
  - Then the ride shows as 12.3 km
  - Example: a ride on 2026-10-28 of 12.25 km, today 2026-10-28 → the page contains `12.3 km`
  - Example (edge): a ride of 1.15 km shows as `1.2 km`
  - Observed at: `render_rides_page` HTML
  - Refines: M2

- **AC-3 The today page shows the day's total distance**
  - Given rides today and on other days
  - When the today page is rendered
  - Then it shows the sum of today's distances only
  - Example: rides on 2026-10-28 of 10.0 km and 2.5 km and one on 2026-10-27 of 7.0 km, today 2026-10-28 → the page contains `Total: 12.5 km`
  - Observed at: `render_today_page` HTML
  - Refines: M3

### Harness Decisions

| Boundary | Harness present? | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Rides page HTML (`render_rides_page`) | pytest (`pyproject.toml:10-12`, `tests/`) | Use as is |
| Today page HTML (`render_today_page`) | pytest (`tests/test_today_page.py`) | Use as is |

### Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] Performance: no change
- [ ] Reliability: existing tests pass, except expectations this design changes
- [ ] Security: not applicable

## Risk Analysis

### Technical Risks

| Risk | Impact | Likelihood | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Float values round unexpectedly | Low | Med | Convert with `Decimal(str(km))`; a test pins 1.15 → 1.2 km |
| A trailing `.0` is lost | Low | Low | Do not `normalize()` the Decimal; a test pins 10.0 → 10.0 km |

### Assumptions

- Distances are positive numbers.

## Open Questions

- None.

## References

- Research: [research.md](research.md)
- Intent: [README.md](README.md)

"""Turns raw ride values into display values."""
from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP


def format_distance(km):
    """Distance as a display string, rounded half up to one decimal, e.g. 12.3 km."""
    if isinstance(km, int):
        return f"{km} km"
    value = Decimal(str(km)).quantize(Decimal("0.1"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
    return f"{value} km"

1	# Test Quality Reference
2	
3	Supporting material for the [test-quality](SKILL.md) rubric: a detector method with worked examples, heuristics for what no linter detects, and the shape of a review finding.
4	
5	## Detector selections
6	
7	This section gives a method that works in any ecosystem, then worked examples of the method for a few stacks. The examples are not a supported list: a stack that is absent from the table (Mocha, node:test, or any other) gets the same method, and skipping the detector step silently because the stack is unlisted hides defects the rubric exists to catch.
8	
9	### Method
10	
11	1. Find the project's own tools. Read the conventions source named at the top of [SKILL.md](SKILL.md) for the linters, test runner, and mutation or coverage tools already in use. Run only what is installed in the project and never install anything, because a tool the team has not adopted produces findings the team cannot act on.
12	2. Select rules by category, using explicit selections rather than the project's configured rule set, because many of the highest-signal rules are off by default and a configured lint run misses them. The core categories the examples cover include: assertion-free tests, always-true or no-op assertions, skipped or focused tests, duplicate tests or titles, stubs of the subject, mocking beyond the subject (any-instance stubs, message chains, stubbed mocks), test-data and setup cost (factory cascades, unneeded persistence), sleeps and wall-clock waits, over-broad exception assertions, and conditional logic in tests. Other rule families a stack's linter offers (for example leaked state, async misuse, oversized snapshots) are selected the same way. Report rules that are available but not enabled separately from violations. Read the lint configuration only for thresholds, and run size rules (such as `RSpec/MultipleExpectations` and `RSpec/ExampleLength`) at the project's thresholds or exclude them, because their defaults conflict with common team guidance.
13	3. Add the runtime checks the stack offers when the conventions source named at the top of [SKILL.md](SKILL.md) gives a runnable command for them: seeded random order, repeat runs on suspect tests only, a slow-test report, a factory or setup-cost profile, and per-test coverage. Run a mutation tool only when that source declares its command. Report any check not run, with the reason.
14	4. Where a category has no detector in the stack, report "no detector for <category> in this stack" and fall back to the rubric and the custom heuristics below, labelled judgment-only. Do not omit the category and do not guess at rule names.
15	5. Include what was found (tools, selections, rules available but not enabled, categories with no detector) in your report, so the testing profile or Testing Conventions can be updated from it and the next run starts from it.
16	
17	### Worked examples
18	
19	These rows show the method applied to six stacks; they are examples, not the only supported stacks. No source publishes false-positive rates for any of these rules; the noise notes are inferences.
20	
21	| Stack | Static selection (default status) | Runtime and suite checks | Known noise |
22	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
23	| RSpec | rubocop-rspec `RSpec/SubjectStub`, `AnyInstance`, `MessageChain`, `StubbedMock`, `NoExpectationExample`, `VoidExpect`, `IdenticalEqualityAssertion`, `UnspecifiedException`, `Be`, `RepeatedExample`, `RepeatedExampleGroupBody`, `LetSetup`, `Focus`, `LeakyConstantDeclaration` (all enabled by default); rubocop-factory_bot `FactoryBot/ExcessiveCreateList`, `FactoryAssociationWithStrategy` (pending) | TestProf `FPROF=1` (total vs top-level factory counts expose cascades), `FDOC=1` (unnecessary persistence), `RD_PROF=1`; `--seed` plus `rspec --bisect`; `mutant --since <ref>` if configured | `MultipleExpectations`, `ExampleLength`, `MultipleMemoizedHelpers`, `NestedGroups` are noisy; `VerifiedDoubles` medium. `FDOC` reports "potential" offenders |
24	| Minitest | rubocop-minitest `Minitest/UselessAssertion`, `AssertWithExpectedArgument`, `UnreachableAssertion`, `TestMethodName`, `DuplicateTestRun` (pending), `NoAssertions` (disabled) | `FPROF` and `FDOC` also work under Minitest | No equivalent of `SubjectStub`; mocking needs the heuristics below |
25	| pytest | `ruff check --select PT,B011,B017 --output-format json`, excluding style-only `PT006`, `PT007`, `PT001`, `PT023` and `S101`. Only `PT010`, `PT014`, `PT020`, `PT025`, `PT026`, `PT031` are enabled by default | `--durations`; pytest-randomly seeded order; pytest-repeat or flakefinder on suspects only; coverage contexts for overlap; mutmut if configured | No assertion-free-test rule and no static sleep rule; the heuristics below fill in |
26	| Jest / Vitest | Recommended: `expect-expect`, `no-conditional-expect`, `no-standalone-expect`, `valid-expect`, `no-identical-title`, `no-disabled-tests`, `no-focused-tests`. Opt-in: `no-conditional-in-test`, `no-large-snapshots`, `require-to-throw-message`, `max-expects` | `--randomize --seed`; Stryker `--incremental` | `expect-expect` misfires on custom assertion helpers until `assertFunctionNames` is set |
27	| Playwright / Testing Library | Playwright recommended covers `no-wait-for-timeout`, `no-force-option`, `no-networkidle`, `prefer-web-first-assertions`; `expect-expect` and `no-unnecessary-assertions` are opt-in. Testing Library `await-async-*`; `prefer-explicit-assert` is opt-in | none listed | Bare `getBy*` asserts implicitly, which confuses `expect-expect` |
28	| Go | testifylint `useless-assert`, `expected-actual`, `require-error` (on by default) | gremlins on small modules | gremlins is still 0.x |
29	
30	The selections come from the rubocop-rspec, rubocop-factory_bot, rubocop-minitest, Ruff, eslint-plugin-jest, @vitest/eslint-plugin, eslint-plugin-playwright, eslint-plugin-testing-library, and testifylint documentation.
31	
32	## Custom heuristics
33	
34	No linter in any ecosystem detects mocking volume or a mirrored oracle. Check these with grep or an AST helper, and present each hit as "review these" with line evidence, because each needs judgment to confirm and has no validated threshold:
35	
36	- stubs of the subject, or of ActiveRecord, outside RSpec;
37	- interaction-only assertions (only `have_received` or `toHaveBeenCalled`-style assertions in a test);
38	- assertions on source text or CSS class strings;
39	- `sleep` or wall-clock bounds;
40	- expected values that call production helpers;
41	- assertion-free tests in Python.
42	
43	## Review finding
44	
45	Each finding from a reviewer or auditor has these fields:
46	
47	- **Verdict**: Remove, Rewrite, Consolidate, or Keep (rubric Part 3).
48	- **Rubric item**: the Part 1 item, or the Part 2 property and item.
49	- **Location**: file:line and a quoted excerpt.
50	- **Evidence type**: deterministic (the named detector, planted defect, or diff) or judgment-only.
51	- **Majority**: for a judgment-only Remove or Rewrite, the majority result (for example 3 of 3).
52	- **Objective evidence**: for Remove or Consolidate, the evidence (no unique killed mutants, or no unique coverage, plus a passing run with the test removed in a disposable worktree), or "judgment-only, not actionable".
53	- **Criterion**: the criterion id, when the review runs inside a plan.
54

All three criteria have an outer test at the right level, each test is green at HEAD, and each one failed when I broke the code it guards. I found nothing to remove or rewrite. Three judgment-only observations are under Review These.

Range: 8659d2a..edc9024 (HEAD); mode: inline
Conventions: the "Testing Strategy" section of `/private/var/folders/8c/t32c953j2qvdpdxh8xjsnrz40000gn/T/tmp.KKYizWtHuO/docs/plans/2026-10-20-rides/tasks.md`. research.md has no Testing Conventions section and there is no `.claude/wb/testing.md`. Drift: `tests/test_today_page.py` has no module-level `TODAY` and uses inline `date(2026, 10, 28)` at lines 7, 13, 14 and 17. The AC-3 test-writer report says it followed the existing file.
Uncommitted changes: none.

Changed test files: `tests/test_rides_page.py` (new), `tests/test_today_page.py`, `tests/test_view_model.py`. Full suite at HEAD: 15 passed.

### Integrity
Findings: 1 (0 escalated)
- Source: step 5 of this review (inline mode).
- **Outer tests vs their red commits:**
  - AC-3: `git diff 8f34716 HEAD -- tests/test_today_page.py` is empty.
  - AC-2: `git diff 576b6a1 HEAD -- tests/test_rides_page.py` is empty.
  - AC-1: `git diff b06a60f HEAD -- tests/test_rides_page.py` shows only the hunk the AC-2 red commit appended (lines 19-28). The AC-1 tests at lines 8-18 are byte-identical to the red commit.
- **Report coverage:** every test change in the phase is named in a test-writer report. The AC-1 and AC-2 outer reports cover `tests/test_rides_page.py`, the AC-3 outer report covers `tests/test_today_page.py:11-18`, and the AC-2 inner report covers `tests/test_view_model.py:9`, `:12-13` and `:16-17`. No change is undeclared.
- **Test hunks:** no skipped or deleted tests, and no expected value is computed by calling the code under test. All expected values are literals from the criteria.
- `tests/test_view_model.py:9`: `assert format_distance(12.25) == "12.3 km"` (was `"12.2 km"`). This changes the expected value of an existing test. Escalated: no.
  - It is declared under "Changes to earlier tests" in the inner report on tmp_KKYizWtHuO-a0e.6.
  - tasks.md asks for it ("Existing expectation: `tests/test_view_model.py:9` ... becomes `"12.3 km"`").
  - It is a unit test, not an outer test.
  - The new value is the literal from the AC-2 example, and the assertion is still an exact equality, so nothing was loosened.
  - The ROUND_HALF_EVEN break (D4 below) makes it fail.

### Criterion Coverage
- **AC-1:** outer tests `tests/test_rides_page.py:8` and `:16`, both calling `render_rides_page` directly (the observed-at level). Red b06a60f; green at HEAD. Breaks that made them fail:
  - D1, `WINDOW_DAYS = 27`: line 12 fails with `assert '2026-10-01' in ...`.
  - D2, `WINDOW_DAYS = 29`: line 13 fails with `'2026-09-30' not in ...`.
  - D3, `<= today` changed to `< today`: line 18 fails.
- **AC-2:** outer tests `tests/test_rides_page.py:21` and `:26`, at `render_rides_page`. Red 576b6a1; green at HEAD. Breaks that made them fail:
  - D4, `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`: line 23 fails with `'12.3 km' in ...12.2 km`.
  - D5, `Decimal(km)` instead of `Decimal(str(km))`: line 28 fails with `'1.2 km' in ...1.1 km`.
  - Each of the two tests is the only outer test that catches its break. Under D4, line 28 still passes, because 1.15 rounds to 1.2 under half-even too.
- **AC-3:** outer test `tests/test_today_page.py:11`, at `render_today_page`. Red 8f34716; green at HEAD. D6, summing `rides` instead of `todays`, makes line 18 fail with `Total: 19.5 km`.

Every failure was an assertion failure, and every break ran in a disposable worktree of HEAD. `git worktree list` afterwards shows only the main tree, and `git status --short` is clean.

### Findings
These are proposals. No test was created, edited, or deleted.

none

Things I checked that came out clean:
- **Doubles:** none in any changed test. All of them call the render function or `format_distance` directly with inline dicts, which matches the declared seam.
- **Copied setup:** `TODAY = date(2026, 10, 28)` appears in `tests/test_rides_page.py:5`, `tests/test_store.py:5` and `tests/test_load_series.py:5`. That one-line constant is what the conventions prescribe, so it is not a finding.
- **Negative assertion:** `tests/test_rides_page.py:13` is anchored by the presence assertion at line 12.

### Majority Candidates
none

### Review These
- **No presence anchor.** `tests/test_today_page.py:8`, `assert "x" not in body`. This is a negative assertion with no positive anchor, so it would pass on an empty body (Part 1 item 4). The test predates the phase and is unchanged, so it is outside the reviewed changes. But it sits in a changed file, and the phase changed the output of `render_today_page`, so it is worth a look. Judgment-only.
- **Inner and outer tests overlap.** `tests/test_view_model.py:9` and `:13` duplicate the AC-2 outer examples one level down.
  - Under D4, only `:9` and its outer twin `tests/test_rides_page.py:23` failed.
  - Under D5, only `:13` and its outer twin `tests/test_rides_page.py:28` failed.
  - None of my planted breaks told an inner test apart from its outer twin. Six hand-planted breaks are not a mutation run, though, and tasks.md asks for these inner cases. They also point to the failing function more directly. So I am not proposing Consolidate. Judgment-only (Specific/Predictive overlap).
- **Two assertions in one test.** `tests/test_rides_page.py:12-13`: one test holds the presence and absence checks, so under D1 the line-12 failure hides line 13. Line 12 is the anchor line 13 needs, and pytest has no aggregate mode here, so this looks acceptable. Judgment-only (Specific, bundled assertions).

### Detectors
- **Tools run:** pytest 9.1.1 only. Ruff is not installed, so I could not run `ruff check --select PT,B011,B017`.
- **Available but not enabled:** none. pytest-randomly, pytest-repeat, coverage and mutmut are not installed. The only other plugin is pytest-playwright 0.10.0.
- **No detector in this stack** for: assertion-free tests, always-true assertions, skipped or focused tests, duplicate titles, stubs of the subject or mocking beyond it, sleeps or wall-clock use, over-broad exception assertions, conditional logic in tests. I grepped the tests for all of these instead (judgment-only):
  - Every changed test has an `assert`.
  - There is no `mock`, `patch`, `monkeypatch`, `skip`, `xfail`, `sleep`, `now(` or `today(` call.
  - No assertion is on a CSS class string.
  - No expected value calls a production helper.

### Mutation
not configured

### Not Run
- **Ruff PT/B selection:** Ruff is not installed in the project.
- **Seeded random order, repeat runs, `--durations`, coverage contexts:** the conventions give no command for them, and pytest-randomly and coverage are not installed.
